A clean, login-free, self-hosted file sharer for Unraid. Open the page, drop a
file, set an expiry, share the link. No accounts, no heavyweight stack.

## Features

- **One-pager upload** — a central drop zone; drop a file and a settings panel
  slides in on the right (expiry + optional password). Upload progress is shown
  as an overlay right on the drop zone. Light/dark toggle.
- **Resumable uploads (tus)** — multi-GB files survive connection drops and
  resume automatically.
- **Per-share expiry** — 1 hour, 6 hours, 1 day, 7 days, 30 days, or never.
  A background job removes expired files and their metadata.
- **Optional password** — scrypt-hashed, never stored in plain text. The
  download streams natively after the password is verified; the permission
  cookie is derived from the server-only hash, so it can't be forged from the
  public link.
- **Share page** — copyable link plus a QR code for phones.

## Architecture

A single container: Next.js (App Router) + Mantine UI, a small custom Node
server that mounts the tus upload handler alongside Next. Files live on a local
volume; metadata sits in one SQLite file (`better-sqlite3`) — no database
server, no login system.

## Running on Unraid

Add the template, map `/data` to your appdata, pick a port. Put it behind a
reverse proxy and set `BASE_URL` (e.g. `https://share.yourdomain.tld`) so share
links use your public domain. `MAX_FILE_SIZE` (bytes, 0 = unlimited) and
`DEFAULT_EXPIRY` are optional.

## Notes

A fresh, much simpler take inspired by Pingvin Share — no backend stack, no
accounts, just drop-and-share.
